metaDescription: Seven portable folding workbenches compared on stated load capacity, built in vise and clamps, bench dogs, frame material, folded size and sawhorse conversion.
expertTake: The BLACK+DECKER Workmate with a 550 lb stated capacity, a bamboo top and a vise is our top pick for a proven, versatile portable bench that clamps almost anything. The WDOT folding bench with bench dogs and a slim fold is the value pick for a small garage or balcony. Skip a light folding bench for heavy hammering or big sheet goods, because a thin frame flexes and a bigger table like the BORA Centipede supports far more.
introParagraphs: A portable workbench gives you a stable work surface that folds away. It holds a board while you saw, clamps a part while you sand and supports a miter saw or a router, and many convert into a pair of sawhorses.

Stated capacity, top size, clamping features and folded size separate the options. Load figures are maker claims for evenly spread weight, not for hammer blows. We evaluated seven models from the candidate pool using spec sheets, listing details and owner feedback patterns, then ranked them by fit for common jobs, not by the biggest capacity number.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER Workmate WM425-A portable workbench, 550 lb capacity, clamps, bamboo top

specList.label: Clamping
specList.value: Adjustable jaws, vertical clamping and four swivel pegs

products.description:
The Workmate is the classic portable folding bench, rated at 550 lb with a heavy gauge steel frame and a laminated bamboo top. Adjustable jaws, vertical clamping and four swivel pegs hold irregular objects as well as boards.

Bamboo is a hard, dense top that resists dents, and the vise action clamps work in a way that few other portable benches can match. Against the Keter, the Workmate has better built in clamping and a smaller top. Against the WORX Pegasus, it offers higher capacity and a vise.

Check the folding hinges and keep the top clean. Oil the vise screws occasionally. Owners often say the Workmate earns its keep by clamping odd shapes, such as a chair leg or a pipe, that an ordinary bench vise cannot hold.
products.bestFor: DIYers and woodworkers who need a movable bench with real clamping.
pros: 550 lb stated capacity with a steel frame
Bamboo top resists dents and wear
Adjustable jaws and pegs clamp odd shapes
Long running design with parts availability
cons: Top is smaller than larger folding tables
Vise jaws limit the size of what you can clamp

products.name: Keter heavy duty folding workbench, 1,000 lb capacity, 12 inch adjustable clamps

specList.label: Setup
specList.value: Ready in about 30 seconds, no assembly

products.description:
The Keter folding workbench is rated at 1,000 lb, has a large work surface and 12 inch adjustable clamps, and sets up in about 30 seconds with no assembly. It suits miter saws and general woodworking.

A 1,000 lb figure is a maker claim, probably for evenly spread weight, but it signals a strong, wide platform. The quick fold system makes it practical for a garage or a site. Against the Workmate, it has a bigger top and fewer clamping options. Against the BORA, it is smaller but cheaper.

Check the legs lock fully before use. Wipe the top and avoid heavy side loads. On a job site, the fast fold is the feature that means it actually gets used, since a bench that is slow to open stays in the van.
products.bestFor: Miter saw stations and large woodworking jobs.
pros: Stated 1,000 lb capacity
Large work surface suits a miter saw
12 inch clamps are included
Sets up in about 30 seconds
cons: Load figure is a maker claim
Fewer clamping features than a vise

products.name: BORA Centipede folding work table 4 x 8 ft portable workbench, 30 inch height, 6,000 lb capacity

specList.label: Feature
specList.value: P-Tops at each contact point protect the workpiece

products.description:
The BORA Centipede is a 4 by 8 foot collapsible work table, 30 inches high, rated at 6,000 lb in the listing, with P-Tops at each contact point to protect the workpiece. It sets up in seconds and packs flat.

A 4 by 8 foot support suits sheet goods such as plywood and drywall, and works as a cutting platform for a track saw or a circular saw. It is a support system, not a flat top bench, because it uses a series of slats and P-Tops that hold the work. Against the Workmate, it is a different tool for big sheets. Against the Keter, it is larger and more specialised.

Check the legs lock and avoid cutting through the top slats. Store flat in a garage. Because it supports a sheet at many points, it keeps the offcut from falling and pinching the blade during a long cut.
products.bestFor: Sheet goods and large cutting jobs.
pros: 4 by 8 foot span supports full sheets
6,000 lb stated capacity
P-Tops protect the workpiece
Sets up and packs flat quickly
cons: No vise or built in clamps
Not a flat bench top for small parts

products.name: WDOT portable folding work bench table 2 in 1, 2 clamps and 6 bench dogs, 500 lb, steel frame

specList.label: Best for
specList.value: Small garages, balconies and car trunks

products.description:
The WDOT 2 in 1 folding bench has a steel frame, an ABS top with pre drilled mounting holes for table saws and routers, two clamps, six bench dogs and a 500 lb stated capacity. It folds to just 5.9 inches thick.

Bench dogs are pegs that fit holes in the top to hold work, which gives it woodworking capability that most plastic benches lack. The slim fold fits small spaces and a car boot. Against the Workmate, it has a plastic top rather than bamboo. Against the Keter, it has dogs and a slimmer fold.

Check the folding mechanism and keep the top free of debris. Tighten the leg bolts. The bench dog holes let you build simple jigs, which opens up proper woodworking on a small folding table.
products.bestFor: Small garages, balconies and mobile work.
pros: Folds to 5.9 inches thick
Two clamps and six bench dogs are included
Pre drilled holes for mounting tools
500 lb stated capacity
cons: ABS top is less hard wearing than bamboo

products.name: WORX Pegasus WX051 portable folding workbench, 2 in 1 table and sawhorse, 31 x 25 x 32 inch

specList.label: Capacity
specList.value: Up to 300 lb as a bench per the listing

products.description:
The WORX Pegasus is a 2 in 1 folding workbench and sawhorse that measures about 31 by 25 by 32 inches, with a stated load capacity of up to 300 lb as a bench. It folds to go anywhere, and a pair of them makes sawhorses for long boards.

A two mode design is ideal for people who only occasionally need a bench. The lower capacity and a smaller top mean it is a light duty tool. Against the Workmate, it has a smaller capacity and less clamping. Against the WDOT, it is a more established brand and more focused on sawhorse use.

Check the locking hinges before loading. Do not overload the sawhorse mode. A pair of them gives you a quick set of sawhorses for breaking down boards and sanding long pieces.
products.bestFor: Occasional use and mobile jobs that need a sawhorse as well.
pros: 2 in 1 workbench and sawhorse design
Folds flat for storage and travel
Known tool brand
Light and easy to carry
cons: 300 lb as a bench is modest

products.name: POWERTEC portable small workbench with vise, ruler and protractor scale, folding sawhorse, 4 bench dogs

specList.label: Clamping
specList.value: Adjustable vise panels and 4 bench dogs

products.description:
The POWERTEC portable bench has a bamboo top, adjustable vise panels, four bench dogs, an imprinted ruler and protractor scale, and a built in storage rack. It is a small, folding sawhorse and worktable.

A built in ruler and protractor help mark cuts, and the vise panels grip small to medium work. The top is small, so it suits hobby projects, not big builds. Against the Workmate, it is smaller with more marking help. Against the WDOT, it has a bamboo top and a vise.

Oil the vise and wipe the top. Check the hinges before loading. The ruler and protractor scales help beginners mark accurate cuts without hunting for a square.
products.bestFor: Small woodworking and hobby projects with built in vise.
pros: Bamboo top with adjustable vise panels
Four bench dogs hold work
Imprinted ruler and protractor aid marking
Built in storage rack for tools
cons: Lower capacity than the Keter or Workmate

products.name: TLGREEN 7 in 1 multifunctional portable workbench with power strip, folds to sawhorse, cart and platform

specList.label: Modes
specList.value: Bench, sawhorse, cart, platform and more

products.description:
The TLGREEN 7 in 1 workstation converts between a workbench, sawhorse, cart and platform, and includes an integrated power strip so lights, chargers and drills can plug in where you work. It aims to replace several pieces of equipment.

A built in power strip is a practical extra for garage work, and multiple modes help with different jobs. As a multi function tool, each mode is a compromise compared with a dedicated one, and the listing gives few capacity numbers. Against the Workmate, it is more versatile and less proven. Against the WORX, it adds a cart mode and power.

Check the locks in each mode and keep the power strip dry. Do not exceed the strip's electrical rating. The power strip is a thoughtful touch, since a work light and a charger often need sockets right where you are working.
products.bestFor: Garage users who want one folding station with power.
pros: Seven modes cover bench, sawhorse and cart
Integrated power strip keeps tools powered
Folds for storage
Flexible for varied jobs

buyingCriteria.explanation: Capacity figures range from 300 lb on the WORX Pegasus to 6,000 lb on the BORA Centipede, and all are maker claims for evenly spread weight. Hammering and dynamic loads are harder on a frame than static weight. Choose a capacity well above your heaviest job. The usual buyer mistake is choosing the highest capacity number and ignoring the size and stiffness of the top.

A larger top supports more, but a smaller top is lighter. Bamboo, as on the Workmate and POWERTEC, resists dents and wear, while ABS and plastic tops are lighter and cheaper. A top with pre drilled holes, as on the WDOT, can mount tools. Think about where you will use the bench: garage floors are rarely level, so adjustable feet help.

A bench with a vise and dogs holds work firmly, which is what makes woodworking safe and accurate. The Workmate has adjustable jaws and pegs, the WDOT has dogs and clamps and the POWERTEC has vise panels and dogs. Without clamping, you need separate clamps. Look for non slip feet or rubber pads, as a bench that slides while you saw is dangerous.

A bench you can store and carry gets used. The WDOT folds to 5.9 inches thick, the BORA packs flat and the Keter sets up in 30 seconds. A heavy steel bench is stable but harder to move. Consider whether you need to mount a tool, since pre drilled holes and a flat top make that possible.

A bench height of about 30 inches suits most people, and some models adjust. Wide feet and non slip pads, as on the WDOT, stop sliding. A wobbly bench is unsafe with saws. Test the folding mechanism if you can, since a fiddly fold means you will leave the bench set up.

A sawhorse mode, a power strip or a ruler scale add convenience. The TLGREEN has seven modes and a power strip, and the WORX converts to a sawhorse. Choose extras you will use, because every extra moving part is a wear point. Buy a couple of extra clamps, because even a bench with a vise rarely has enough clamping for a whole project.

specDecoder.meaning: The weight a bench is rated to hold, usually spread evenly. It does not cover impact or hammering loads.
specDecoder.watchFor: The BORA lists 6,000 lb and the WORX 300 lb, so match it to your work.

specDecoder.meaning: Pegs that fit holes in a bench top to hold work against a vise or clamp.
specDecoder.watchFor: The WDOT includes six and the POWERTEC four.

specDecoder.meaning: A hard, dense top made from bonded bamboo strips. It resists dents and wear.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Workmate and POWERTEC use it, but it can warp if left wet.

specDecoder.meaning: Protective pads at the contact points of the BORA table that protect the workpiece.
specDecoder.watchFor: The BORA uses them, but they wear with cutting.

specDecoder.meaning: A design that works as both a bench and a sawhorse.
specDecoder.watchFor: The WORX and WDOT list it, but check capacity in sawhorse mode.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and build
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated capacities from 300 to 6,000 lb and steel frames against plastic tops. We treated figures as maker claims and did not load test. Owner feedback patterns about wobble, broken hinges and warped tops shaped our scoring.

howWeEvaluated.title: Clamping features
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at vises, clamps, dogs and pegs. Better clamping scored higher for woodworking. We treated capacity figures as maker claims, and noted where the listing said they apply only in certain modes.

howWeEvaluated.title: Size and portability
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed top size, folded thickness and setup time. Benches that store compactly scored higher. We compared folded thickness and weight to judge storage and carry.

howWeEvaluated.title: Extras
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered sawhorse modes, power strips and ruler scales. Useful extras scored higher. Clamping features were weighed more heavily than raw capacity.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We reviewed hinge wear, top durability and owner feedback patterns about wobble. Established brands scored higher. Top material was judged by likely durability in a garage.

cards.label: Vise bench
cards.text: The Workmate, POWERTEC and WDOT clamp work and suit woodworking.

cards.label: Table
cards.text: The Keter and BORA offer bigger, flatter supports for saws and sheet goods.

howToChoose.note: Choose a vise bench for clamping and a table for sawing big material.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A hard top, a vise or clamps, bench dogs and a stable frame. Heavy hammering needs a sturdier bench.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Workmate and POWERTEC have bamboo tops with vises, and the WDOT adds bench dogs.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You work on large pieces often or need a very stable platform. The Keter or BORA suit that.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You do light DIY. The WORX or POWERTEC are enough.

maintenance.why: A loose hinge can collapse under load. Tighten or replace worn parts.
Dust and sawdust jam vise screws. A little oil keeps them smooth.
Moisture warps bamboo and wood. Store indoors and wipe up spills.
Vibration loosens bolts and the bench wobbles. Tighten them with a wrench.
A saw cut damages the top and the clamping surface. Use a sacrificial board.

faq.q: How much capacity do I need?
faq.a: For general DIY, 300 to 550 lb is plenty. Heavy work, such as large table saws and masonry, needs more and a sturdier bench. Many owners say that a thin sheet of sacrificial plywood on the top protects the surface and makes clamping easier.
They are maker claims for evenly spread weight, not for impacts. Treat them as a guide and stay well below them. Check the legs are fully locked every time you set the bench up.
Pegs that fit holes in the bench top and hold work against a vise or clamp. They are common in woodworking benches. Keep the bench on level ground and add shims if the floor slopes.

faq.q: Can I use a folding bench with a table saw?
faq.a: Only if the maker says so and the bench is stable. Many have pre drilled holes for tools, but a table saw needs a solid platform. Do not stand on a folding bench, as it is not designed for a person's weight in that way.
Bamboo is harder and resists dents, while plastic is lighter and cheaper. Bamboo needs to be kept dry. Use a mallet or a rubber hammer for light tapping and avoid heavy blows to the top.
In a dry place, folded flat. Moisture and damp harm wood tops and rust frames. Wipe the top regularly to prevent glue and resin build up.
